description: "Passionate innovators and problem solvers united to tackle global challenges using NASA's open data. Ready to brainstorm, build, and push our limits during this hackathon!"
summary:
**Building a Glasshouse on Mars**

Our project aims to design a sustainable glasshouse on Mars to support human life and enable long-term scientific research. We developed a protective living environment that addresses Mars's challenging conditions, including high radiation, low atmospheric pressure, extreme temperatures, and limited energy resources.

The glasshouse combines UV-protective and radiation-resistant materials, pressure control systems, airlock doors, and an AI-powered monitoring system to ensure astronauts' safety and comfort. It uses solar panels and geothermal energy from the Elysium and Tharsis regions to generate electricity. Additionally, an oxygen production system inspired by NASA's MOXIE technology helps provide breathable air.

This project is important because it aims to reduce dependence on Earth by providing essential resources such as oxygen, energy, and a controlled environment for growing plants. Ultimately, our design could become a foundation for sustainable human settlements and future communities on Mars.
details:
Project Details

What does it do and how does it work? Our project designs a sustainable, high-tech glasshouse for Mars to enable long-term human habitation and research. It functions as a controlled ecosystem providing vital life-support:

  • Radiation Protection: Uses UV-shielded, polymer-infused glass to block cosmic radiation.
  • Atmospheric Pressure & Seals: Features integrated air compressors to maintain human-safe indoor pressure,alongside airlock doors to prevent contamination.
  • Oxygen & Atmosphere Control: Uses an electrolysis-driven system (inspired by NASA's MOXIE) to extract oxygen from Martian CO2CO2​ (56.3 kWh/day) and maintains a 78% nitrogen atmospheric balance (15.4 kWh/day).
  • Dual Energy Grid: Powered by a 100 m2m2 solar array generating 7–145 kWh/day (depending on dust storm conditions) combined with Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) in volcanic hotspots like Tharsis and Elysium generating a reliable 75.6 kWh/day. Total daily production spans from 82.6 kWh to 220.6 kWh, comfortably covering the base 78.3 kWh daily operational load.

What benefits does it have & intended impact? The glasshouse allows astronauts to grow fresh food, produce breathable oxygen, and conduct scientific research safely. By providing a stable microclimate and natural vegetation, it enhances both physical health and psychological comfort. It establishes a scalable, cost-effective framework (estimated project budget between $16.5K and $2.17M) for future modular settlements and self-sufficient Martian cities.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used:

  • AI & Automation Systems: Monitored by a central artificial intelligence that dynamically balances indoor heating,tracks climate shifts, and alerts crew members to structural breaches or mechanical failures.
  • EGS Geothermal & MOXIE-inspired Tech: Geothermal energy harvesting in volcanic provinces and solid oxide electrolysis for oxygen extraction.

Creativity & Team Considerations: Our creative solution pairs dynamic solar harvesting with geothermal energy to overcome Mars's infamous dust storm vulnerabilities, guaranteeing power even during global storms. Our team carefully considered atmospheric toxicity, extreme temperature fluctuations, radiation risks, human psychological well-being, and strict energy budgets to build a practical, budget-conscious step toward off-world colonization.
